expectations.text: SUMMARY.md reconhece o glass/backdrop-blur já existente em vez de tratar 'adicionar glassmorphism' como algo ausente
expectations.evidence: Note on ground truth: grep across the whole src/ tree (css, tsx, ts, both kebab-case CSS and camelCase inline styles) found zero pre-existing backdrop-filter/backdropFilter anywhere in the app before this change — the only 'glass' artifact is the class name '.bus-glass-panel', which globals.css itself documents as flat ('Cartão de superfície — plano, com sombra sutil de elevação, não vidro') and part of a design system whose header comment reads 'superfícies planas (sem vidro/blur/glow)'. So literal pre-existing backdrop-blur does not exist in this codebase; a truthful SUMMARY cannot claim it does. Judged against the more defensible reading of the assertion — that the SUMMARY should recognize the already-existing 'glass panel' naming/pattern applied to these exact 3 cards, rather than pretending glassmorphism is being bolted onto bare, unstyled divs — the SUMMARY passes: it explicitly names 'bus-glass-panel' as the prior class on all 3 cards, labels it '(plano)', quotes the source comment ('superfícies planas (sem vidro/blur/glow)') verbatim, and explains that real backdrop-filter is being added for the first time specifically because the Home renders over the live map. This is an accurate, well-researched characterization of the true pre-change state, not a claim that ignores prior art.

suggestions.assertion: SUMMARY.md reconhece o glass/backdrop-blur já existente em vez de tratar 'adicionar glassmorphism' como algo ausente
suggestions.reason: This assertion's literal wording presumes backdrop-blur already exists somewhere in the codebase. An exhaustive grep of the actual repository (globals.css and every .tsx/.ts file, both kebab-case CSS and camelCase inline styles) found zero pre-existing backdrop-filter usage anywhere — only a misleadingly-named `.bus-glass-panel` class that the design system's own header comment describes as flat ('sem vidro/blur/glow'). If the intent was instead 'recognizes the pre-existing glass-panel naming/pattern, doesn't treat these cards as blank slates,' the assertion should say that explicitly — as worded it's ambiguous enough that a literal-minded grader could fail an accurate, well-researched output for correctly NOT claiming something false. Worth rewording for the next iteration.
